newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine delegation to seek Bonn aid - sources.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine delegation to seek Bonn aid - sources.

text.p: A group of Ukrainian officials is due to travel to Bonn next week seeking aid for the cash-strapped country, Western sources said on Friday.
"An official delegation has been invited by the German Finance Ministry. The meeting is for next Friday," one source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
A second western source confirmed the trip was planned.
Ukrainian ministry officials were not available for comment.
Deputy Finance Minister Mykhailo Honcharuk said last week Ukraine was seeking foreign help to restructure its $3.5 billion debt to Russia, mostly for energy costs.
There has been no official confirmation that Ukraine has any plans to sell its debt, though the Financial Times reported it was trying to sell $350 million of it to German banks.
The delegation could also be seeking to collect on a one billion mark ($600 million) loan discussed when Chancellor Helmut Kohl visited Kiev last September, one of the sources said.
But such talks might produce few results given budgetary tightening in Germany, a western economist said.
About $1.4 billion was rescheduled in 1995 to cover outstanding debt to Russia's Gazprom.

A further subject for talks could be the launching this week of a criminal investigation by President Leonid Kuchma into how about 87 million marks ($51 million) from a German government grant went missing.
It was part of a 400 million mark grant, given by Bonn in 1994 and intended for victims of the Nazis during World War Two. It disappeared in a struggling Ukrainian bank.
